required_fixes: Provenance mismatch: committed analyze.py (sha256 c2a085bb9f632ab7faf9ccaad5582cf21edd7b4433c47c6b96bf9b2166347d15) does NOT generate the derived artifacts result.json/analysis_results.json. Running it on the frozen raw evidence produces 8 measurements (duplicate cart_1 not deduplicated), computes densities over ALL roles (not per-definition filtering for DEF-FULL-MAP / DEF-FORM-ONLY / ISOLATED-A-LINK), yields truncated ordering cart>detail>product_listing -> full product_listing>detail>cart and C3 random_lower=False, verdict FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING, contradicting the stored verdict SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. The script that generated the 3-definition analysis_results.json was not committed. Commit the exact script that produces the 3-definition output and deduplicates cart_1 to 7 tasks, or mark current analysis_results as exploratory.

C3 decision cherry-picking: spec.json decision_rule condition (3) and prereg 9.1 require random baseline lower bias across all tasks; prereg 6.4 defines random simulation per task. Producer reports c3_random_baseline_lower=true based only on primary definition DEF-FULL-MAP (mean trunc 0.2921 vs random 0.2888) while hiding that DEF-FORM-ONLY fails for all 7/7 tasks (mean trunc 0.004773 vs random 0.006596, random higher). Falsification rule is 'ANY condition fails => FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING'. Under frozen rule, C3 fails for DEF-FORM-ONLY, so conjunctive SURVIVES fails if definitions are treated symmetrically. Either preregister primary-definition-only C3 or report C3 as MIXED and bound the claim to a->link-inclusive definitions.

Full-DOM estimator validity: result.json validity_notes correctly states full-DOM uses raw DOM tag counts (dom_stats.linksCount 393-397, not locatable). Locatable/total_dom ratio is 0.048 (listings), 0.023-0.024 (details), 0.018 (cart). Using total DOM counts as locatable counts inflates full density ~6-7x for listings and ~20x for cart relative to locatable-scaled bound (linksCount * locatable/total_dom ≈19 scaled locatable <a> for listings vs 393 raw). Report 98.2-98.6% relative bias and absolute densities 0.29 must be relabeled as UPPER BOUNDS, not point estimates. Recompute and display locatable-scaled alternative: DEF-FULL-MAP scaled bias ≈69% listings, 48-51% details, 14.5% cart; DEF-FORM-ONLY scaled bias ≈68% listings, 60% details, 0% cart; ordering under scaled model remains cart>detail>product_listing? Actually scaled ordering becomes product_listing>detail>cart, still a swap but taxed.

Bias magnitude denominator inconsistency: prereg 6.2 defines relative bias as (full-trunc)/trunc but result.json and analysis_results.json compute relative_bias as (full-trunc)/full (abs_bias/full). For listing_clothing DEF-FULL-MAP 0.2878/0.2929=0.982 vs 0.2878/0.00516=55.7 (5570%). Producer's c2 threshold >20% uses full-denominator; under trunc-denominator all 7 tasks exceed 5000%. Standardize definition and rerun threshold check explicitly.

Ordering change fragility and small-N: Page-type ordering change (cart>product_listing>detail -> cart>detail>product_listing) rests on near-tied means: truncated product_listing 0.005135 vs detail 0.004280 (Δ0.00085, 20%) and full product_listing 0.29296 vs detail 0.29871 (Δ0.0057, 2%). With n=3 listings, 3 details, 1 cart, no within-type variance or CI is reported; cart n=1 cannot estimate variance. The swap is not tested for statistical distinguishability. Add per-page-type SD/CI and note cart ordering is underpowered.

Random baseline construction circularity and trivial effect: random baseline pool composition is inferred from same inflated DOM proportions (a=62/82 listings via scaling) and uses with-replacement draws (analyze.py:96 replace=True). Even under producer model the advantage is tiny: mean abs bias 0.2921 vs 0.2888 Δ0.0033 (≈1.1% relative), well within simulation noise (1000 draws, seed fixed). Report effect size and p-value for truncation vs random difference; do not claim document-order bias is confirmed on ~1% mean difference.

Deduplication not preregistered: raw evidence contains 8 valid measurements including duplicate cart_1 (two runs 2026-09-12T23:08:13 and 23:08:16, both locatable 21, identical payload). Producer deduplicates to 7 by keeping last, but prereg 5.1 and provenance n_measurements_valid=7 do not state deduplication rule. Document rule and verify that ordering/bias are stable whether using first, last, or averaged duplicate.

Positive control redefinition: spec positive_control states a->link reversal must be preserved in full-DOM ordering if bias drives effect; producer's observed ordering swaps product_listing and detail (cart remains #1) and then claims pass because swap confirms truncation drives effect. This inverts the frozen expectation. Clarify control: either the ordering must change (as evidence of bias) or be preserved (as evidence of robustness) — not both — and evaluate pass/fail accordingly without post-hoc inversion.

claim_ceiling: Truncation bias is real and page-type-ordering-relevant, but only at a bounded ceiling: (1) First-20 document-order truncation discards 62-95% of locatable elements (82->20 listings, 32->20 details, 21->20 cart) and biases a->link-inclusive interactive density; (2) Ordering between product_listing and detail swaps when correcting with DOM counts (cart>product_listing>detail -> cart>detail>product_listing for DEF-FULL-MAP, product_listing>cart>detail -> product_listing>detail>cart for DEF-FORM-ONLY) — this direction is reproducible under both inflated-DOM and locatable-scaled estimators, but the swap magnitude is small (full means within 2% for inflated model; scaled model shows even smaller absolute densities 0.016 vs 0.008) and based on n=1 cart and n=3 per other type on a single Magento site, so not statistically distinguished; (3) Bias magnitude is NOT 98% as a locatable-dense point estimate — proper locatable-scaled bound is ~69% listings, ~48-51% details, ~14% cart for DEF-FULL-MAP; DEF-FORM-ONLY shows minimal bias for cart (0-1.6%); (4) Random-baseline advantage is trivial (~1% mean) and definition-dependent (fails for DEF-FORM-ONLY), so document-order vs sample-size attribution is not discriminated; (5) Ordering stability and null-model 0.3 vs 0.52 question remains UNRESOLVED pending full-DOM locatable enumeration in runtime lane (parent handoff blocking substrate). Do not claim truncation catastrophically invalidates all density metrics at 98% or that the parent FALSIFIED verdict is explained — claim only that the a->link-inclusive ordering is sensitive to enumeration and that existing truncated data cannot support a locatable-density claim without the substrate fix.
